lessons.title: Find the sentence that tells you
lessons.strategy: The answer is written in the text. Pick the key word in the question, then find the sentence with that word.
lessons.tip: Put your finger on the sentence that answers the question.

steps: The question asks about the pot. The key word is pot.
Find pot in the text: 'Ravi has a tomato plant in a blue pot.'
The word just before pot tells the colour. The pot is blue.

lessons.title: First, next, last
lessons.strategy: A story tells things in order. Words like first, then, after and at last show the order.
lessons.tip: Find the event in the question, then read the sentence that comes next.

worked.prompt: What did Ravi do after he picked the tomato?
worked.answer: He and his sister ate it with salt.
steps: Find the event in the question: 'He picked the tomato'.
Read the next sentence: 'Then they ate it with salt.'
The word Then shows this came next. They ate the tomato with salt.

lessons.title: Look for because
lessons.strategy: A why question asks for a reason. The word because often comes just before the reason.
lessons.tip: Find because. The reason is the words after it.

worked.prompt: Why did Ravi pick the tomato?
steps: Find the sentence about picking: 'He picked the tomato because it was ripe.'
The words after because give the reason: it was ripe.

lessons.title: Actions show feelings
lessons.strategy: Writers often show a feeling instead of naming it. Look at what the person does, and ask: when do people do that?
lessons.tip: Find the action first. Then name the feeling behind it.

worked.prompt: How did Ravi feel when the tomato turned red?
steps: The text does not name the feeling. Look at what Ravi did.
'Ravi jumped up and down and called his sister.'
People jump up and down and call others when they are excited. Ravi was happy and excited.

lessons.title: What is it all about?
lessons.strategy: The topic fits every sentence of the text. A detail fits only one sentence.
lessons.tip: Ask: does this answer fit the whole text, or only one line?

worked.prompt: What is this text mostly about?
steps: Look at each sentence. Almost every one is about the plant or its tomato.
Salt comes in only one sentence, so salt is a detail.
The answer that fits the whole text is Ravi's tomato plant.

lessons.title: Can you check it?
lessons.strategy: A fact can be checked. An opinion is what someone thinks or feels, and other people may not agree. Words like best, nicest and more fun are clues.
lessons.tip: Ask: could we look and check this? If people could disagree, it is an opinion.

worked.answer: Tomatoes are the best food in the world.
steps: 'By Friday the tomato was red.' We could look at the tomato and check. It is a fact.
'Tomatoes are the best food in the world.' Someone else may like mangoes more.
Best is a clue word. People can disagree, so this sentence is an opinion.

passages.title: Ravi's Tomato Plant
passages.text: Ravi has a tomato plant in a blue pot. Every morning he gives it water. On Monday he saw one small green tomato. By Friday the tomato was red. Ravi jumped up and down and called his sister. He picked the tomato because it was ripe. Then they ate it with salt. Tomatoes are the best food in the world.

passages.title: The Late Bus
passages.text: Anu goes to school by bus. The bus is yellow. Today the bus came late because one tyre was flat. Anu waited at the stop for a long time. She looked at her watch again and again and tapped her foot. At last the bus came. Anu got in and sat next to her friend Leela. A bus is more fun than a car.

questions.prompt: What colour is the bus?
questions.evidence: The bus is yellow.
questions.explain: The second sentence says the bus is yellow.
questions.hint: The key word is bus. One short sentence tells its colour.

questions.prompt: What did Anu do after the bus came?
questions.right: She got in and sat next to Leela.
questions.evidence: Anu got in and sat next to her friend Leela.
questions.explain: 'At last the bus came' is followed by 'Anu got in and sat next to her friend Leela.' The watch and the waiting came before.
questions.hint: Find 'At last the bus came.' What does the very next sentence say?

questions.prompt: Why did the bus come late?
questions.evidence: because one tyre was flat
questions.explain: The text says the bus came late because one tyre was flat.
questions.hint: Find the word because in the text.

questions.prompt: How did Anu feel while she waited?
questions.evidence: She looked at her watch again and again and tapped her foot.
questions.explain: People look at a watch again and again and tap a foot when they want something to hurry up.
questions.hint: What did Anu do with her watch and her foot? When do people do that?

questions.prompt: What is this text mostly about?
questions.right: the day Anu's bus came late
questions.evidence: Today the bus came late
questions.explain: Almost every sentence is about the bus coming late and Anu waiting. Leela and the tyre each come in one sentence.
questions.hint: Which answer fits nearly every sentence, not just one?

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an opinion?
questions.right: A bus is more fun than a car.
wrong: Anu goes to school by bus.
questions.evidence: A bus is more fun than a car.
questions.explain: Some people think a car is more fun. We cannot check it, so it is an opinion. The other two can be checked.
questions.hint: Which sentence could someone disagree with? Look for the words more fun.

passages.title: The Paper Boat
passages.text: It rained all night. In the morning there was a big puddle near the gate. Mani made a paper boat. First he folded the paper. Next he drew a flag on it. Then he put the boat on the water. The boat sank because the paper got wet. Mani's lips shook and he rubbed his eyes. His father made a new boat with him. Rainy days are the best days.

questions.prompt: Where was the puddle?
questions.evidence: there was a big puddle near the gate
questions.explain: The second sentence says the puddle was near the gate.
questions.hint: The key word is puddle. Find the sentence with that word.

questions.prompt: What did Mani do first?
wrong: He put the boat on the water.
questions.evidence: First he folded the paper.
questions.explain: The word First tells us: he folded the paper. The flag came next and the water came after that.
questions.hint: Look for the words First, Next and Then.

questions.prompt: Why did the boat sink?
questions.evidence: because the paper got wet
questions.explain: The text says the boat sank because the paper got wet.
questions.hint: Find the sentence with sank. Read the words after because.

questions.prompt: How did Mani feel when the boat sank?
questions.evidence: Mani's lips shook and he rubbed his eyes.
questions.explain: Shaking lips and rubbing eyes show someone is about to cry. Mani was sad.
questions.hint: What did Mani's lips and eyes do? When does that happen to people?

questions.prompt: What is this text mostly about?
questions.right: Mani's paper boat on a rainy morning
questions.evidence: Mani made a paper boat.
questions.explain: Most sentences are about the boat: making it, floating it, and making a new one.
questions.hint: Count how many sentences are about the boat.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an opinion?
questions.right: Rainy days are the best days.
questions.evidence: Rainy days are the best days.
questions.explain: Some people like sunny days more. Best is a clue word. The other two sentences can be checked.
questions.hint: Look for a clue word like best.

passages.title: The New Puppy
passages.text: Meena got a puppy on Sunday. The puppy is white with one black ear. At first it hid under the bed because it was scared. Meena put some milk in a bowl. Slowly the puppy came out and drank the milk. Then it licked Meena's hand. Meena laughed and clapped her hands. She named the puppy Dot. Puppies are the nicest pets.

questions.prompt: When did Meena get the puppy?
questions.evidence: Meena got a puppy on Sunday.
questions.explain: The first sentence says Meena got the puppy on Sunday.

questions.prompt: What did the puppy do after it drank the milk?
questions.evidence: Then it licked Meena's hand.
questions.explain: After 'drank the milk' the text says 'Then it licked Meena's hand.' Hiding came earlier.

questions.prompt: Why did the puppy hide under the bed?
questions.evidence: because it was scared
questions.explain: The text says it hid under the bed because it was scared.

questions.prompt: How did Meena feel when the puppy licked her hand?
questions.evidence: Meena laughed and clapped her hands.
questions.explain: People laugh and clap when they are happy.

questions.prompt: What is this text mostly about?
questions.evidence: Meena got a puppy on Sunday.
questions.explain: Every sentence is about the puppy. The milk and the bed are small details.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an opinion?
wrong: Meena got a puppy on Sunday.
questions.evidence: Puppies are the nicest pets.
questions.explain: Some people think cats are nicer. Nicest is a clue word. The other sentences can be checked.

passages.title: Sports Day
passages.text: Today was Sports Day at Arun's school. Arun ran in the first race. He fell down because his shoelace was open. He got up, tied his lace and ran again. He came last. Arun looked down at the ground and did not talk to anyone. Then his teacher gave him a star for not giving up. Arun's school has two hundred children. Running is the most exciting sport. Sports Day is better than any other day.

questions.prompt: What did the teacher give Arun?
questions.evidence: his teacher gave him a star
questions.explain: The text says his teacher gave him a star for not giving up.

questions.prompt: What did Arun do just after he fell down?
questions.right: He got up and tied his lace.
questions.evidence: He got up, tied his lace and ran again.
questions.explain: The sentence after the fall says he got up, tied his lace and ran again. Coming last and the star were later.

questions.prompt: Why did Arun fall down?
questions.evidence: because his shoelace was open
questions.explain: The text says he fell down because his shoelace was open.

questions.prompt: How did Arun feel when he came last?
questions.evidence: Arun looked down at the ground and did not talk to anyone.
questions.explain: Looking down and not talking to anyone shows that Arun was sad.

questions.prompt: What is this text mostly about?
questions.evidence: Arun ran in the first race.
questions.explain: Most sentences are about the race: the fall, running again, coming last and the star.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a fact?
questions.right: Arun's school has two hundred children.
wrong: Running is the most exciting sport.
Sports Day is better than any other day.
questions.evidence: Arun's school has two hundred children.
questions.explain: We could count the children and check. The other two say what someone thinks, with the clue words most exciting and better.

passages.title: Grandma's Garden
passages.text: Grandma has a small garden behind her house. She grows beans, chillies and roses. Every evening she waters the plants. Yesterday a goat came in because the gate was open. The goat ate three rose plants. Grandma put her hands on her head and shouted. Then she shut the gate and tied it with a rope. Now the goat cannot come in. Roses are the prettiest flowers.

questions.prompt: Where is Grandma's garden?
questions.evidence: Grandma has a small garden behind her house.
questions.explain: The first sentence says the garden is behind her house.

questions.prompt: What did Grandma do after she shouted?
questions.right: She shut the gate and tied it with a rope.
questions.evidence: Then she shut the gate and tied it with a rope.
questions.explain: After the shouting, the text says 'Then she shut the gate and tied it with a rope.'

questions.prompt: Why could the goat come into the garden?
questions.evidence: because the gate was open
questions.explain: The text says a goat came in because the gate was open.

questions.prompt: How did Grandma feel when the goat ate her roses?
questions.evidence: Grandma put her hands on her head and shouted.
questions.explain: People put their hands on their head and shout when they are upset.

questions.prompt: What is this text mostly about?
questions.evidence: Yesterday a goat came in
questions.explain: The text tells about the garden and what happened when the goat came in. Beans and the rope are small details.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an opinion?
wrong: She grows beans, chillies and roses.
The goat ate three rose plants.
questions.evidence: Roses are the prettiest flowers.
questions.explain: Some people find other flowers prettier. Prettiest is a clue word. The other two can be checked.

passages.title: The Tiffin Box
passages.text: Kavin takes a tiffin box to school every day. Today he could not find it in his bag. He left it at home because he was in a hurry. At lunch time Kavin sat alone and held his stomach. His friend Sara saw him. She gave him two of her idlis. After lunch they played catch. An idli is made from rice. Idlis are tastier than dosas. Sharing is the best thing a friend can do.

questions.prompt: What did Sara give Kavin?
questions.evidence: She gave him two of her idlis.
questions.explain: The text says she gave him two of her idlis.

questions.prompt: What did Kavin and Sara do after lunch?
wrong: They looked for the tiffin box.
questions.evidence: After lunch they played catch.
questions.explain: The words After lunch tell us: they played catch.

questions.prompt: Why did Kavin leave his tiffin box at home?
wrong: He did not like the food.
questions.evidence: because he was in a hurry
questions.explain: The text says he left it at home because he was in a hurry.

questions.prompt: How did Kavin feel at lunch time, before Sara came?
questions.evidence: Kavin sat alone and held his stomach.
questions.explain: Sitting alone and holding his stomach shows he was hungry and unhappy.

questions.prompt: What is this text mostly about?
questions.right: Kavin forgot his lunch and a friend shared hers
questions.evidence: She gave him two of her idlis.
questions.explain: The text is about the forgotten tiffin box and Sara sharing her food. The other answers are small details.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a fact?
questions.right: An idli is made from rice.
wrong: Sharing is the best thing a friend can do.
questions.evidence: An idli is made from rice.
questions.explain: We can check what an idli is made from. Tastier and best show what someone thinks.
